findings.title: Journal search builds SQL with string formatting: an apostrophe causes a 500 error, and SQL can be injected
findings.where: GET /api/journal?q=… and the /journal page search box
findings.steps: On /journal, type O'Brien (or any text containing ') into Search, or open /journal?q=O'Brien. Or curl /api/journal?q=O'Brien.
findings.expected: Normal search results (or none) with a 200 response; the search term is bound as a parameter and LIKE wildcards are escaped (escape_like already exists in routers/common.py).
findings.actual: The API returns 500 Internal Server Error and the page shows 'Could not load the journal.' The input goes straight into SQL: q=%' OR 1=1 OR ' returns every entry, so any SQL can be injected.
findings.evidence: curl ?q=O'Brien -> 500; curl ?q=%25' OR 1=1 OR ' -> 200 with all entries; the page showed 'Could not load the journal.' Code: backend/routers/journal.py clauses.append(f"(j.body LIKE '%{term}%' ...")

findings.title: Search treats % and _ as wildcards
findings.expected: Only entries that contain that character literally.
findings.actual: Every entry comes back as a match.
findings.evidence: curl ?q=_ returned all entries; escape_like is never used.

findings.title: Journal error states have no retry
findings.where: /journal page and the Journal section of /plants/:id
findings.steps: Make GET /api/journal fail (mocked a 500, or search with an apostrophe). Open /journal, or open a plant from the Plants list.
findings.expected: An error message plus a Retry button that loads the data again once the server is back.
findings.actual: Only the alert 'Could not load the journal.' appears. There is no retry control, so the user has to reload the page. On the plant page, the badge still says '3 entries' while the list failed to load.
findings.evidence: Plant section text: 'Journal / 3 entries / … Entries, newest first / Could not load the journal.' with no button. The journal page is the same.

findings.title: Adding an entry spins forever when the request hangs (no 10 s timeout)
findings.where: /plants/:id New entry form (also Save entry when editing, and Delete)
findings.steps: Make POST /api/journal never answer, type text and click Add entry, then wait more than 10 s.
findings.expected: The request times out after 10 s, shows an error and re-enables the button with the text kept.
findings.actual: The button stays on 'Saving…' and disabled for good. useApiClient/useApiFetch set no timeout.
findings.evidence: After 13 s the form text was still 'Saving…'.

findings.title: Character counter and limit count UTF-16 units, so emoji entries cannot be edited
findings.steps: Create an entry of 500 emoji (the server accepts it, since Python counts code points), then click Edit and Save entry.
findings.expected: The counter and limit agree with the server: 500 characters, and the entry saves.
findings.actual: The counter shows '-500 characters left' and saving fails with 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' The textarea maxlength also stops new entries at about 250 emoji.
findings.evidence: Edit form text: '-500 characters left' and then 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' after Save.

findings.title: Very large IDs return 500 instead of 4xx
findings.actual: 500 Internal Server Error (SQLite integer overflow). The same pattern exists elsewhere in the app.

findings.title: Implausible dates such as year 0001 are accepted
findings.expected: A lower bound (for example after 1900) that refuses the date with a reason.
findings.actual: 201 Created; the entry is stored and shown as 1 Jan 0001 at the bottom of the list.
